llm.summary: This is a coherent Guangdong procurement-data skill, but users should understand its API-key storage and optional device-based auto-registration flow.

dimensions.detail: External calls to the vendor API are expected; if no API key exists, auto-registration is disclosed as consent-gated and collects platform, CPU architecture, and a SHA-256 MAC hash.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package is Markdown documentation only, with no executable installer, dependency bootstrap, background service, or remote-code execution mechanism in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Most instructions are scoped to querying the vendor API, but the docs contain inconsistent default-region and amount-unit guidance, and company-name expansion may broaden results without confirmation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill reads ZLBX_API_KEY or ~/.zlbx/config.json and, after consented auto-registration, writes the returned API key to ~/.zlbx/config.json; it does not install hooks, scheduled tasks, or system-level persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's tender search, company lookup, market analysis, account balance, and API authentication behavior fit its stated procurement-data purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending procurement queries to Zhiliaobiaoxun and storing an API key locally. To avoid device-feature collection, configure ZLBX_API_KEY or ~/.zlbx/config.json yourself before first use. When using the skill, verify the stated search region and amount units because the documentation has inconsistent examples.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] expected: The auto-registration/device-feature collection concern is real but disclosed, limited to missing-key onboarding, and requires user consent before collection or network transmission.
[SDI-1] expected: Account provisioning is broader than pure data querying, but it is directly tied to obtaining access to the API and includes a manual-key alternative.
[E1] expected: The external POST to the registration endpoint sends disclosed device features to the same vendor service used by the skill, not a hidden or unrelated destination.
[RA2] expected: Persisting the API key in ~/.zlbx/config.json is credential persistence, but it is documented and used for subsequent authenticated API calls rather than stealthy session control.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The conflicting Guangdong-versus-national default and amount-unit guidance are documentation quality issues that can affect query accuracy, but they do not show malicious behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Automatic expansion from a shorthand company name to related entities supports group-level procurement analysis, though users should confirm scope when names are ambiguous.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language documentation matches the China/Guangdong procurement domain; it is a usability limitation rather than evidence of unsafe agent behavior.
